description: Is valid UTF-8 encoded JSON per RFC 8259. Duplicate JSON object keys within any object make the document non-conformant. A leading byte-order mark makes the document non-conformant. Note: RFC 8259 section 8.1 forbids adding a byte-order mark, and tolerating one would let two parsers disagree over the same bytes. Rejecting duplicate names follows interoperable-JSON practice (RFC 7493 section 2.3); most JSON parsers silently keep one duplicate value, so checking the duplicate clause requires a duplicate-detecting parse.
notes: Inline documents cover ordinary parsed values; documentText preserves duplicate keys and malformed JSON; documentBase64 carries exact bytes for invalid UTF-8 and a forbidden leading byte-order mark. Runners must hand the selected carriage to the strict document parser without pre-normalizing it.

tests.description: OBI document exercising several JSON value types
duplicate root object key is invalid even when both values are individually valid
duplicate key nested inside an operation object is invalid
leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is forbidden
invalid UTF-8 byte sequence is refused before JSON interpretation

a leading byte-order mark makes the text non-conformant through OBI-D-01 alone: OBI-D-02 to OBI-D-13 impose no further requirement on it and hold vacuously (a tool records them as satisfied or not applicable), so the dependency on a missing operation adds no violation (section 10, The document and its data)

a repeated operations member makes the text non-conformant through OBI-D-01 alone, whichever value a parser keeps: OBI-D-02 to OBI-D-13 impose no further requirement on it and hold vacuously (a tool records them as satisfied or not applicable) (section 10, The document and its data)
